part.carlsbad.title: Carlsbad and the minority attack
part.carlsbad.summary: In the Carlsbad structure, White advances the a- and b-pawns against Black's three queenside pawns and leaves a weak pawn on c6 or d5.
ex.cb.LxJcC: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.LxJcC.hint: The black pawn on c6 is on the file of your rook on c7. Count the black king's squares: which ones are already watched by your pawns and the bishop?
ex.cb.LxJcC.solution: 47.Rxc6#! The rook captures the c6-pawn with check. The king has no free square: e5 and f5 are watched by the pawns, e7 and g7 by the bishop, and e6 and g6 by the rook. It is mate.
ex.cb.v8jLd: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.cb.v8jLd.hint: Here the roles are reversed: the white pawn on c3 is on the half-open c-file, attacked by the queen and the rook on c8. Who defends it, besides the king?
ex.cb.v8jLd.solution: 21...Qxc3#! The queen captures the c3-pawn with check, defended by the rook on c8, and the king cannot recapture. It has no free square either: it is mate.
ex.cb.UdXbA: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.UdXbA.hint: The structure is Carlsbad, but the black king has no pawns in front of it. Your queen on h6 watches f8, g7 and h7. What can your rook on the f-file do?
ex.cb.UdXbA.solution: 32.Rxf8#! The rook captures the one on f8 with check, defended by the queen on h6. The king cannot recapture, and f7, g7, h7 and h8 are watched: it is mate.
ex.cb.7rxWS: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.7rxWS.hint: The black king is on b8, behind the b7-pawn. Which white pieces aim at the b7-square?
ex.cb.7rxWS.solution: 33.Qxb7#! The queen captures the b7-pawn with check, defended by the knight on c5. The king cannot recapture and has no free square: it is mate.
ex.cb.dTP87: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.dTP87.hint: The black pawn on c6 is on the half-open c-file, and only the b7-pawn defends it. What opens if the b7-pawn leaves the b-file?
ex.cb.dTP87.solution: 15.Nxc6! The knight captures the c6-pawn and attacks the queen on d8 and the rook on b8. After 15...bxc6, the b-file opens, and 16.Qxb8 captures the rook.
ex.cb.luAYM: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.luAYM.hint: The black pawn on c6 is backward, and only the rook on b6 defends it. What happens if that rook leaves b6?
ex.cb.luAYM.solution: 20.Rxb6! The rook captures the one on b6, which defended the c6-pawn. After 20...axb6, 21.Qxc6 captures the backward pawn and attacks the rook on a8.
ex.cb.oiseI: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.oiseI.hint: The black pawn on c6 has no b-pawn beside it and no piece defending it. Which black piece stands on the same file, further down?
ex.cb.oiseI.solution: 21.Rxc6+! The rook captures the c6-pawn with check and attacks the bishop on c2 along the c-file. After 21...Kd7, 22.Rxc2 captures the bishop.
ex.cb.BoyFn: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cb.BoyFn.hint: The black pawn on c6 is backward, and both your rooks attack it along the c-file. Count its attackers and defenders.
ex.cb.BoyFn.solution: 33.Rxc6+! The rook captures the c6-pawn with check. The bishop on b7, its only defender, recaptures, and 34.Rxc6+ captures it, again with check. After 34...Kd7, 35.Bxd5 also captures the d5-pawn.
ex.cb.5NmVQ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.cb.5NmVQ.hint: The white bishop on e4 is close to your d5-pawn. Who attacks that bishop, and who defends it?
ex.cb.5NmVQ.solution: 12...dxe4! The d5-pawn captures the bishop on e4, which only the knight on c3 defended. After 13.Nxe4, 13...Rxe4 captures the knight along the e-file: Black captures two pieces for a pawn.
part.maroczy.title: Maróczy and Hedgehog
part.maroczy.summary: With the White pawns on c4 and e4 against the Black d6 pawn, White squeezes with the space, and Black waits for the moment to advance a pawn.
ex.mz.68NbY: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.mz.68NbY.hint: Your knight occupies the d5 square, and the Black king on g8 is hemmed in by its own pieces. The h6 bishop watches f8 and g7.
ex.mz.68NbY.solution: 20.Nxe7#! The d5 knight captures the e7 pawn with check. The g8 king has no square: f8 and g7 are watched by the h6 bishop, and the others are taken by Black pieces.
ex.mz.viALc: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.mz.viALc.hint: With no d-pawn, the d3 square has only White pieces to defend it. The White queen on d2 is on the same diagonal as the e1 king and your queen.
ex.mz.viALc.solution: 14...Nd3#! The c5 knight goes to d3 with check. The d2 queen cannot capture it: it is pinned by your a5 queen. The e1 king has no free square.
ex.mz.1Qht9: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.mz.1Qht9.hint: Your knight occupies the d4 square, next to the White king on e3. The king is hemmed in by its own pieces and by yours.
ex.mz.1Qht9.solution: 33...Nc2#! The d4 knight goes to c2 with check, and the e3 king has no free square: it is mate.
ex.mz.mGQqM: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.mz.mGQqM.hint: The Black queen and a rook stand on the fifth rank, with one square between them. Which of your pawns can reach that rank?
ex.mz.mGQqM.solution: 21.b4! The pawn attacks the a5 queen and the c5 rook at the same time. After 21...Qb6, 22.bxc5 captures the rook.
ex.mz.ss0SN: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.mz.ss0SN.hint: The Black d6 pawn is isolated and attacked twice. Also look at where the Black king is.
ex.mz.ss0SN.solution: 28.Bxd6+! The bishop captures the d6 pawn with check. After 28...Qxd6, 29.Rxd6 captures the queen: the d7 knight blocks the d-file, and the d8 rook cannot recapture.
ex.mz.9OqFD: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.mz.9OqFD.hint: The Black d6 pawn has no pawn to defend it, and your two rooks are on the d-file, behind it. Only the c5 bishop and the king defend it.
ex.mz.9OqFD.solution: 27.Rxd6+! The rook captures the d6 pawn with check. After 27...Bxd6, 28.Rxd6# the other rook recaptures with check, and the d7 king has no square: it is mate. 28.Qxd6+ also wins, but without the mate.
ex.mz.fXOyl: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.mz.fXOyl.hint: Your e4 pawn stands between the g2 bishop and the Black bishop on c6. The Black queen is on f6.
ex.mz.fXOyl.solution: 18.e5! The pawn advances, attacks the f6 queen and, by leaving e4, opens the diagonal of the g2 bishop to the c6 bishop. After 18...Qxe5, 19.Bxc6 captures the bishop.
ex.mz.95kP8: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.mz.95kP8.hint: The White knight occupies the d5 square, and only your f6 knight attacks it. After capturing on d5, your knight is attacked: look for a square from which it attacks two pieces.
ex.mz.95kP8.solution: 13...Nxd5! The knight captures on d5 and opens the diagonal of the b2 bishop to your g7 bishop. After 14.Bxg7, 14...Nf4 attacks the d3 queen and the e2 bishop at the same time: the knight escapes, and Black is a piece up.
